summary: A 1978 description of MARS, a Message Archiving and Retrieval Service developed at Computer Corporation of America using the Datacomputer, a network database utility.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 744 describes MARS, a service for archiving network messages and searching them later. Users file messages by mail and send retrieval requests to another mailbox.

questions: how did early networks archive messages
how do you search an archived message collection
subtitle: A mail-based service for filing messages and retrieving them by indexed fields.

tldr.problem: Groups and individual users needed a way to archive messages and retrieve them later using selected information.
tldr.mechanism: MARS files messages sent to MARS-Filer, indexes message fields and text, and accepts retrieval requests sent as mail to MARS-Retriever.
tldr.outcome: The RFC documents the MARS service, its filing modes, retrieval fields, and access distinctions between public and private messages.

today: RFC 744 documents the MARS service developed at Computer Corporation of America using the Datacomputer. It describes its operation and user procedures as of publication.

sections.title: Message Collections and Indexes
sections.content:
MARS uses the Datacomputer to store and retrieve messages. It supports public messages, which anyone may retrieve, and private messages, which may be retrieved by the archiver or named recipients.

The Filer creates indexes from message sections, including addresses and dates, subject words, and body text. The RFC describes retrieval using combinations of criteria.
sections.plainLanguage: MARS stores messages in collections and indexes information from their headers and text. Public and private messages have different retrieval permissions.

sections.title: Filing Messages
sections.content:
A user files a message by sending it to MARS-Filer using ordinary message tools. The RFC describes single-message filing, forwarding a message to the Filer, and batch filing with a batch marker in the subject.

For forwarded messages, annotations added to the forwarding envelope are filed and retrieved with the archived message. Batch messages are handled as a series of individual messages.
sections.plainLanguage: Users can send one message, forward a message, or bundle several messages for filing. Notes added to a forwarded message become part of the archived material.

sections.title: Retrieving Messages
sections.content:
A retrieval request is a specially formatted message sent to MARS-Retriever. Its body can specify DATE, AFTER, SINCE, BEFORE, UNTIL, FROM, TO, SUBJECT, and TEXT criteria.

The RFC defines how combinations are interpreted: for example, multiple names in FROM are ORed, while spaces and commas in TO, SUBJECT, and TEXT imply AND unless OR is written explicitly. Matching messages are mailed back one at a time.
sections.plainLanguage: A user writes search fields in a message and sends it to MARS-Retriever. MARS sends matching archived messages back to the requester's mailbox.

sections.title: Background Processing
sections.content:
The Filer checks for mail every hour, and the Retriever checks every quarter-hour. The RFC says the intervals can be changed to meet demand and that the service is intended to run as a background job during low-activity periods.

The document also describes an interactive TENEX program for composing retrieval requests.
sections.plainLanguage: MARS checks for filing and retrieval requests periodically rather than continuously. Users can also use the described interactive program to prepare a retrieval request.
